source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (Regional Final)
source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question A2

prompt: Let $T=36$. The curve with equation $y=x^2+x$ cuts the line with equation $y=2x+\sqrt T$ at two points. Find the sum of the $y$ co-ordinates of these points.

solutions.title: Intersect
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from A1.) With $\sqrt T=6$, solving $x^2+x=2x+6$ gives $x^2-x-6=0$, so $x=3$ or $x=-2$. The corresponding $y=2x+6$ values are $12$ and $2$. Their sum is $14$.

**Answer: $14$**

solutions.title: Sum of roots
solutions.body:
Eliminate $x$ instead: from the line $x=\frac{y-6}2$, and the curve gives $\left(\frac{y-6}2\right)^2+\frac{y-6}2=y$, i.e. $(y-6)^2+2(y-6)=4y$, i.e. $y^2-14y+24=0$. The sum of the roots (the two $y$ co-ordinates) is $14$.

**Answer: $14$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (Regional Final)
source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question A3

prompt: Let $T=14$. The length of a rectangle is $3$ cm more than its width. The perimeter of the rectangle is $3T$ cm. The length of a second rectangle is $2$ cm more than its width. The perimeter of this rectangle is $(T+10)$ cm. The difference in the areas of these rectangles is $k\ \text{cm}^2$. Find $k$.

solutions.title: Find both rectangles
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from A2.) First rectangle: perimeter $42$, so width $w$ satisfies $2(2w+3)=42$, $w=9$, length $12$, area $108$. Second: perimeter $24$, so $2(2w+2)=24$, $w=5$, length $7$, area $35$. The difference is $108-35=73$.

**Answer: $73$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (Regional Final)
source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question A4

prompt: Let $T=73$. The operation $\diamond$ is defined by $a\diamond b=\dfrac{a+b+ab}{a+b}$. The value of $\left(\dfrac{T-3}{10}\right)\diamond(6\diamond3)$ is $\dfrac pq$, where $p$ and $q$ are positive integers with no common factor other than $1$. Find $p-q$.

solutions.title: Evaluate
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from A3.) Note $a\diamond b=1+\frac{ab}{a+b}$. Then $6\diamond3=1+\frac{18}9=3$ and $\frac{T-3}{10}=7$. So the value is $7\diamond3=1+\frac{21}{10}=\frac{31}{10}$, giving $p-q=31-10=21$.

**Answer: $21$**

source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question B2

prompt: Let $T=6$. The equation $x^2+(T-1)x-T=0$ has solutions $x=a$ and $x=b$, where $a<b$. Find $a$.

solutions.title: Factorise
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from B1.) $x^2+5x-6=(x+6)(x-1)=0$, so the solutions are $-6$ and $1$; $a=-6$.

**Answer: $-6$**

source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question B3

prompt: Let $T=-6$. A rectangle has sides of length $(11+T)$ cm and $(7-T)$ cm. The area of the rectangle is $A\ \text{cm}^2$ and the perimeter is $P$ cm. Find $A-P$.

solutions.title: Substitute
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from B2.) The sides are $5$ and $13$, so $A=65$ and $P=2(5+13)=36$. Then $A-P=29$.

**Answer: $29$**

source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question B4

prompt: Let $T=29$. $T$ can be written as $a^2+b^2$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive integers with $a>b$. Let $K=(a+b)^3-(a-b)^3$. Find $K$.

solutions.title: Find $a$ and $b$
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from B3.) $29=25+4=5^2+2^2$ is the only way, so $a=5$, $b=2$ and $K=7^3-3^3=343-27=316$.

**Answer: $316$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (Regional Final)
source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question C1

prompt: $Y$ is inversely proportional to $X^2$. $Y=36$ when $X=8$. Find the value of $Y$ when $X=16$.

solutions.title: Scale
solutions.body:
Doubling $X$ multiplies $X^2$ by $4$, so $Y$ is divided by $4$: $36/4=9$.

**Answer: $9$**

source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question C2

prompt:
Let $T=9$. The frequency table for a variable $x$ is shown below.

| $x$ | $2$ | $4$ | $6$ | $8$ | $10$ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| frequency | $T+3$ | $T$ | $2T-7$ | $T\div3$ | $T-4$ |

The mean value of $x$ is $m$. Find $m$.

solutions.title: Weighted mean
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from C1.) The frequencies are $12,\,9,\,11,\,3,\,5$, total $40$. The sum of $x$ values is $2\cdot12+4\cdot9+6\cdot11+8\cdot3+10\cdot5=24+36+66+24+50=200$. So $m=200/40=5$.

**Answer: $5$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (Regional Final)
source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question C3

prompt: Let $T=5$. The sum of the interior angles of a regular polygon is $10(2T-1)(3T+1)$ degrees. Find the number of sides of this polygon.

solutions.title: Angle sum formula
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from C2.) $10\cdot9\cdot16=1440=180(n-2)$, so $n-2=8$ and $n=10$.

**Answer: $10$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (Regional Final)
source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question C4

prompt: Let $T=10$. A bag contains $T-4$ red counters and $T-6$ blue counters. Four counters are withdrawn at random, one after another, without replacement. $p$ is the probability that exactly three of the withdrawn counters are red; $q$ is the probability that exactly two are red. The ratio $p:q$ may be written in the form $a:a+1$, with $a>0$. Find $a$.

solutions.title: Count selections
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from C3.) There are $6$ red and $4$ blue counters. Choosing $4$ counters (all equally likely subsets), exactly three red: $\binom63\binom41=80$; exactly two red: $\binom62\binom42=90$. So $p:q=80:90=8:9$ and $a=8$.

**Answer: $8$**

source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question D2

prompt: Let $T=64$. A bag contains $10$ counters. There are $\left(\dfrac{T-4}{10}\right)$ red counters in the bag. All the other counters in the bag are blue. Three counters are removed at random without being replaced. The probability of there being exactly two counters of the same colour among the three that have been removed is $\dfrac ab$, where $a$ and $b$ are positive integers with no common factor other than $1$. Find $a+b-1$.

solutions.title: Complement
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from D1.) There are $6$ red and $4$ blue counters. Among three counters of two colours, exactly two of the same colour occurs unless all three have the same colour. $P(\text{all red})+P(\text{all blue})=\frac{\binom63+\binom43}{\binom{10}3}=\frac{20+4}{120}=\frac15$. So the required probability is $\frac45$, $a+b-1=4+5-1=8$.

**Answer: $8$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (Regional Final)
source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question D3

prompt: Let $T=8$. The decagon shown has rotational symmetry of order $5$. The size of angle $BCD$ is $4T^\circ$. The obtuse angle $ABC$ is $x^\circ$. Find the sum of the digits of $x$.

solutions.title: Interior angles of the star decagon
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from D2.) Angle $BCD=32^\circ$ is an interior angle at one of the five outer points, and by symmetry all five outer angles equal $32^\circ$. The five inner vertices have equal reflex interior angles $r$. The interior angles of a decagon sum to $8\cdot180=1440$, so $5\cdot32+5r=1440$, $r=256$. The angle $ABC$ marked at an inner vertex is the obtuse (non-reflex) angle $360-256=104$, and $1+0+4=5$.

**Answer: $5$**

source.contest: UKMT Senior Team Maths Challenge (Regional Final)
source.paper: 2018-19 Regional Final, Shuttle Round, question D4

prompt: Let $T=5$. The simultaneous equations $x^2+6xy+9y^2=49$ and $x^2+4xy+4y^2=T^2$ have four pairs of solutions. $n$ is the sum of the two positive values of $x$ that occur in these solutions. Find $n$.

solutions.title: Take square roots
solutions.body:
(In the contest $T$ was the answer passed on from D3.) The equations are $(x+3y)^2=49$ and $(x+2y)^2=25$, so $x+3y=\pm7$ and $x+2y=\pm5$. Then $y=(x+3y)-(x+2y)$ and $x=3(x+2y)-2(x+3y)$, so the four sign choices give $(x,y)=(1,2),\ (-29,12),\ (29,-12),\ (-1,-2)$. The positive values of $x$ are $1$ and $29$, so $n=30$.

**Answer: $30$**
